source.title: Exploring OpenAI's Latent Directions: Tests, Observations, and Poking Around

record.tranche_reason: The post qualitatively evaluates native GPT2-SMALL neurons against SAE directions by checking whether top activations match concepts in text. This differs from the Qwen pole audit and does not estimate the same interpretability shares.
record.gate_note: The post reports manual concept-matching results for GPT2-SMALL neurons and SAE directions. The searches and layer counts are results, not merely parameter choices. The red example is a qualitative comparison; it does not provide a proportion of interpretable neurons.
record.test_reason: The post manually inspects top activations of native GPT2-SMALL MLP neurons and judges whether they are monosemantic or match concepts in a query text. This is weakly relevant to V2 (neuron interpretability in another dense LM). The selection and match criterion differ from a pole audit, so no share of one-job neurons can be read.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author concludes SAE directions were consistently and significantly better than neurons at identifying concepts, though worse in later layers. The author also states no monosemantic red neuron was found and that neurons were 'a disaster' in the Odyssey search.
record.recipe_differences: The post searches OpenAI GPT2-SMALL SAE directions and native neurons, then manually checks top activations against concepts in selected text. It does not perform a pole-level audit using the original audit's method.
record.method_sensitivity: Layer affected direction match counts: they ranged from 25 in layer 0 to 7 in layer 11. Excluding layer 0 reduced direction matches from 25 to 22.

fits_no_version.finding: OpenAI SAE directions matched text concepts better than native neurons in every layer of GPT2-SMALL. Direction match counts fell from 25 (layer 0) to 7 (layer 11). A red-specific direction was found but no red-specific neuron.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In GPT2-SMALL, SAE latents are more monosemantic than MLP neurons under top-activation inspection, with the advantage shrinking in later layers.

record.problems: Exploratory manual assessment; the Odyssey evaluation uses one selected text and top-result counts, and the post notes that the randomized literary query could have produced a different snippet. No uncertainty estimates or controls are reported. The probes do not estimate the population share of interpretable neurons.
record.rows_left_out: No reported claim-relevant results left out. The per-layer neuron result for the all-layers-except-layer-0 condition is not stated, so no numeric row is available for it.

untested.parts: No estimate of one-job, two-job or unexplained neuron shares. Only GPT2-SMALL; no other sizes, no MoE, no large-scale models. No random sample of neurons.

record.verdict_notes: Exploratory blog post with a single text and manual judgement, no controls and no uncertainty reported. The per-layer denominator of 25 is implied, not stated.

versions.untested_parts: No Qwen3-32B audit or estimates of pole-level job counts.

The study tests only GPT2-SMALL with qualitative concept-matching probes. It does not estimate shares of one-job, two-job, or unexplained neurons, or test other model sizes, MoE models, or models up to trillions of parameters.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron or recursive-generalization test.
No comparison of architecture, regularization, or tools, and no estimates for InceptionV1-sized vision models.
The post does not systematically test neuron explanations against held-out activation examples.
No automated scoring of explanations by simulated activations on new text.

relationships.reason: Few neurons matched (4/25 all layers; 3/25 in layers 10-11) and the author calls many non-matches highly polysemantic. This is weak, indirect evidence against clean neurons in a small older model; it gives no share (r1, r3-r14).
relationships.display_finding: Only 4 of 25 top results matched across all layers, and 3 of 25 in layers 10–11. The author calls many non-matches highly polysemantic, but this is weak, indirect evidence and gives no overall share.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: GPT2-SMALL MLP neurons, search-ranked top-25 results on one Odyssey snippet, token-match criterion
labels.reason: Few neurons matched (4/25 overall), and per-layer counts run from 3 to 17. This is weak, indirect evidence. The reason text says '3/25 in layers 10-11', but the text gives 3 for layer 10 and 3 for layer 11 separately.

relation.reason: The post reports its own results on neuron interpretability in GPT2-Small, though its criterion is not a pole audit.

tranche.reason: New setting (GPT2-Small neurons, informal search and token-match check) with a weak result bearing on V2. T2 is also arguable.

source_check.notes: Matches compare top tokens on one text, a weak proxy for 'one main job'. The all-layer 4/25 and the per-layer counts come from different search scopes. The table shows neurons 13 vs directions 12 at layer 8 (tied at 9), though the author says directions were better in every layer.

statements.correction: All-layer top-25 neurons: 4 matched, and most of those 4 also fired on unrelated tokens. Per-layer neuron matches: 17 (layers 0 and 6) down to 3 (layer 10) and 3 (layer 11), each a separate count. Author: most non-matches lacked matching tokens or were highly polysemantic (example 11:2172).
statements.problem: '3 of 25 in layers 10-11' reads as one combined count, but the text gives 3 for layer 10 and 3 for layer 11 as separate per-layer counts. 'Many' non-matches called highly polysemantic goes further than the text: the author says most non-matches either lacked matching tokens or were highly polysemantic, and gives one example.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Native neurons gave few matches in the Odyssey probe and no monosemantic red neuron was found; directions performed better. These qualitative probes do not estimate neuron interpretability shares. Rows r1, r3-r14, r27, and r29.
